title: Floquet Theory — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Floquet Theory's rich face: the theory page's own tests, laid beside the sections they test — the unit circle (gathered from the Floquet project's face), the three ways a multiplier leaves it and what each one makes, the Bloch and Floquet sides computed by methods that share nothing, and the Kapitza pendulum's rule held against its multipliers. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: /Projects/Floquet Time-Modulated Loops/Floquet Time-Modulated Loops — rich — multipliers.html
pieces.title: one period, two multipliers · from the Floquet project's face
pieces.caption: **The unit circle, tested.** Made for [[Floquet Time-Modulated Loops]] on the same equation, and gathered here because it tests this list: one pump period carries a circle of starting states onto an ellipse of the same area (det M = 1); the two multipliers ride the unit circle until they meet at −1 or +1 and split; and the test, with and without damping. With no damping the stable pair sits on |ρ| = 1, not inside it, so “|ρ| < 1: stable” is the damped case. Its text says “the page”, meaning the Floquet project's; the claim is the same.
pieces.near: The unit circle in the complex plane is the dividing line

pieces.file: Floquet Theory — rich — three ways out.html
pieces.title: three ways out of the circle
pieces.caption: **What each crossing makes, heard and measured.** One damped ring at 220 Hz and its two multipliers; the pump at 440 Hz pushing one out at −1 (below, at and above q = 0.0050); the ring at 440 Hz and the pump pushing one out at +1 (q = 0.200); a pair that the pump can turn but never move, until the damping goes negative; and the test, 24 runs read on a stroboscope. Every growth matches its multiplier to 4 × 10⁻⁵ a period. At −1: a tone at 220.00 Hz that flips side every look, the period doubled. Off the axis: its own pitch, 340.3 Hz, and a closed curve of looks, a torus. At +1: one point per run, on + in 4 runs of 8 and on − in 4, two mirror rings born together: a pitchfork here, not the transcritical the text names. Every run is rendered in the page and played as drawn.

pieces.title: Stage 1 · q = 0.05, labelled below threshold
pieces.caption: With the build's damping (ζ = 0.025) the threshold is q = 2ζ = 0.05, so this one sits on it: a hiss wandering between about −47 and −25 dB. Even here, one pump period on the signal is its own negative (correlation −0.998).
pieces.near: Each of these has a characteristic audible signature

pieces.title: Stage 1 · q = 0.10, labelled at threshold
pieces.caption: Twice the threshold: full within 0.2 s, steady at −10 dB. The tone is 220.00 Hz, half the 440 Hz pump; the pump's own rate stands 93 dB down and the harmonics are odd only (660 Hz at −31 dB), because the wave flips sign every pump period (correlation −1.000). This is the period doubling the sentence promises.
pieces.near: Each of these has a characteristic audible signature

pieces.title: Stage 1 · q = 0.30, well above
pieces.caption: Full within 0.1 s, steady at −5 dB, still 220.00 Hz with odd harmonics only (660 Hz at −20 dB). The three files share one gain, so their levels compare.
pieces.near: Each of these has a characteristic audible signature

pieces.file: Floquet Theory — rich — same equation twice.html
pieces.title: same equation, read twice
pieces.caption: **The duality, checked by two methods that share no code.** A wave in a cosine lattice; the same numbers relabelled as a pumped spring, where one look per cell or per period turns by one angle, k for Bloch and the quasi-frequency for Floquet; the bands from plane waves beside the growth from integration; and the test. Gap edges from the plane-wave matrix and tongue edges from the integrator agree within 2 × 10⁻⁷, and inside the bands tr M / 2 = cos kπ within 4 × 10⁻¹². Odd gaps open at the zone edge with a negative multiplier (the period-doubling tongues), even ones at the centre with a positive one. It also pins the dictionary: k stands for Im μ, not μ, and the energy for a.

pieces.file: Floquet Theory — rich — standing on a shake.html
pieces.title: standing on a shake
pieces.caption: **Kapitza's pendulum, and how fast is enough.** A 20 cm rod balanced upside down falls (×1.150 every fiftieth of a second); shaken 2 cm at 5 Hz it still falls; at 50 Hz it stands and wobbles, its multipliers on the unit circle; and the test, every stroke and rate decided by one shake period's multipliers, with Kapitza's rule (hΩ)² > 2gL drawn over. For a short stroke the rule is the whole story (onset 15.80 Hz against 15.76 at h = L/10). Past a stroke of 0.454 L the standing band has a top: at h = L/2 it stands only from 3.30 to 6.71 Hz, and the full swing agrees (stands at 6 Hz, falls at 12). No friction anywhere.

offers.what: “|ρ| < 1: stable” and “|ρ| = 1: marginal, the stability boundary” describe a damped system. For the undamped Mathieu equation, and any system with det M = 1, which the page's own Hamiltonian paragraph describes, a stable state has both multipliers on |ρ| = 1: measured, 941 of 941 stable a on q = 0.3 at |ρ| = 1 within 6 × 10⁻⁹, and the standing Kapitza pendulum the same. The boundary there is where the pair meets at ±1 and splits. Suggest naming both cases: with damping, all inside means it decays; with none, all on the circle and apart means it stays bounded. The Philosophical Lens's “Re(μ) < 0: stable” is the same damped reading; whether to touch a quoted voice is a taste call.

“ρ → +1: transcritical bifurcation” names a special case. Generically a multiplier at +1 is a fold (saddle-node) of periodic orbits; transcritical and pitchfork need extra structure. In this resonator, which has no preferred sign, crossing the edge of tongue 2 is a pitchfork: the state at rest goes unstable and two mirror rings appear together. Measured, 8 runs from 8 whispers at q = 0.35: every run holds one stroboscope point, 4 on + and 4 on −. Suggest “ρ → +1: a fold in general; transcritical or pitchfork when the system has the structure for it (a symmetric resonator gives a pitchfork)”.

The complex-pair crossing can't be reached by pumping a single resonator. With a 2 × 2 monodromy, ρ₁ρ₂ = det M = e^(−κT) is fixed by the damping, and a pair off the axis shares one size, so the pump turns it but never moves it out: measured, |ρ| = e^(−κπ/2) to 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ for q from 0 to 0.3 at κ = ±0.005. Only negative damping (a ring that feeds itself) or a system with more degrees of freedom gives that crossing. Suggest one clause saying so, since the next sentence promises later stages will make it audible. Not measured here: that with two or more degrees of freedom a Hamiltonian system's pairs can also collide off the real axis (a Krein collision, the combination resonance), which would qualify the Hamiltonian paragraph's “the only way out”; true of the Mathieu equation as written.

“The Floquet exponent μ has replaced Bloch's crystal momentum k” is off by a factor i: inside a band μ = ik, so what stands for k is Im μ, the quasi-frequency β, and what stands for the energy E is a, the pitch squared. “The quasi-energy spectrum β(μ)” then reads better as a against β at fixed q, which is the band structure exactly. Measured: at the plane-wave energies for k = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, tr M / 2 = cos kπ within 4 × 10⁻¹², and gap edges equal tongue edges within 2 × 10⁻⁷. Two things the page could add: for the Mathieu equation the duality is an identity, since it is the wave equation in a cosine lattice word for word; and odd gaps open at the zone edge with negative ρ, so Bragg reflection at the zone edge is the period-doubling tongue.

“Stable when its pivot is vertically oscillated fast enough” holds for a short stroke and not a long one. Kapitza's rule, top speed hΩ above √(2gL), matches the multipliers within 0.2 % at a stroke of L/10 (15.80 Hz against 15.76). Past a stroke of 0.454 L, where the first Mathieu tongue crosses a = 0 at q = 0.908, the standing band has a top: at h = L/2 the pendulum stands only from 3.30 to 6.71 Hz, and the full nonlinear swing agrees (stands at 6 Hz, falls at 12 Hz). Suggest “fast enough, its top speed above √(2gL), with a stroke small beside the rod”.

For the Floquet project, not this page: static/11_bloch_floquet_duality.png, which the nomination listed for this section, was left off the face. Its band panel draws the bands as straight crossing lines with no gap opened (the one yellow “gap” is a line at E ≈ 0.16); its gain panel shades about eight narrow “tongues” between ω ≈ 0.27 and 0.75 where the gain is only ripple around zero; and its footer maps k ↔ μ and E ↔ ω, where the measured dictionary is k ↔ Im μ and E ↔ a = ω². Read from the image, not re-rendered. The made piece stands in for it.
